answer: The ember multiplier is published, charged in pulse, and kernel lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2614 identities would post 3536 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
